label: late original-phase positions and the <DEL> step (positional ramp, encoding phase only)
explanation: Positional encoding-phase feature. Never fires at t<3 or anywhere in the copy phase (t>L). In the original phase its rate climbs with absolute position: 6% at position 3, 31% at 4, 58% at 5, 75-81% at 6-8. At the <DEL> step it fires 58% of the time (28% of activation mass). Activation also builds within a sequence, usually peaking at the last original token or at <DEL>. Magnitude depends on content: sequences whose early tokens include s/v/w/c/j/f give the highest activations (first_tok in that set has 94% precision but low recall), and first occurrences of a token fire more often than repeats (26% vs 4%). The top examples peak on h at position 6-7. The predicate (original or delimiter step, t>=5) catches about 90% of activation mass, but around 30% of the steps it marks are inactive, mostly sequences without those early letters. Loosening to t>=4 raises mass recall to 0.99 but drops precision to 0.58.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: s, v, w, c, j, f; least: 2, m, 1, h) and the current input token, by step (t=3: h, 1, l, 2; t=4: h, l, 2, 1; t=5: h, 1, l, 2); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, t=7.
